---
title: "10 · Interpretation and responsible application"
description: "Working out what a model has learned, and what you can honestly claim from it in a paper."
categories: [interpretation, reproducibility, uncertainty]
---

A model that predicts well has not thereby explained anything. It has found patterns
that are useful for prediction, which may be causal, may be proxies, and may be
artefacts of how the data were collected. A habitat model can achieve excellent
accuracy by learning where the survey vessels went.

This final section is about the step between having a model and making a scientific
claim: working out which features actually drive the predictions, deciding whether an
interpretable model would serve you better than an accurate black box, reporting the
work so that someone else could repeat it, and being straight about uncertainty.

It is the section that determines whether the work holds up in review — and after.

## In this section

- Feature importance and model interpretation
- Black-box models versus interpretable models
- Reproducibility and transparent reporting
- Communicating uncertainty and limitations
- Practical marine-science examples and exercises
